values.goal: Build Three.js scenes with React components, and manage frame values, selection state, and shared resource lifetimes separately.
values.capstone: A 3D learning scene with selection and notes, a comparison of individual mesh objects and instancing, demand behavior verification, and a resource ownership report.

values.title: Declarative Scenes
values.prerequisites: React state, ref, Effect and cleanup; Three.js geometry, material, and cameras; vectors and delta.
values.environment: Use JSX in a separate React Vite project. Record compatible major versions of React and @react-three/fiber, the Three.js version, and the lockfile. This course uses stable WebGL-based APIs and does not mix in alpha WebGPU APIs. Handle frame updates with useFrame and ref. The existing react-three-fiber-01 preview is a starting point. Implement the extended deliverables described here in a separate project.
values.concepts.0.title: React renderer
values.concepts.0.explanation: R3F represents Three.js objects as a React tree. A mesh inside Canvas is not a DOM element; a separate renderer manages it.
values.concepts.1.title: Object Ownership
values.concepts.1.explanation: The geometry and material declared in JSX are attached to the scene tree. When passing objects created externally, check who is responsible for their lifetime.
values.outcomes.0: The corresponding code for the cube, camera, and lights is recorded.
values.outcomes.1: Changing scale changes the cube size.
values.steps.0: Install compatible React, Three.js, and @react-three/fiber versions in an external React Vite project, and record them.
values.steps.1: Declare a mesh, boxGeometry, meshStandardMaterial, and lights inside Canvas in src/Scene.jsx.
values.steps.2: In notes/day01.md, map the existing imperative cube creation, addition, and removal code to JSX.
values.variables.0.name: scale prop
values.variables.0.expected: The displayed cube becomes larger while using the same geometry.
values.criteria.0: The corresponding code for the cube, camera, and lights is recorded.
values.criteria.1: Changing scale changes the cube size.
values.questions.0: Why does putting an ordinary div inside Canvas cause problems?
values.questions.1: What objects do a mesh declaration and geometry creation produce?
values.references.0.title: R3F Getting Started and React Version Compatibility

values.title: Canvas Size and Camera
values.prerequisites: Unit 2 continues using the deliverables and experiment records from Unit 1.
values.environment: First check the execution scope guidance on the example screen. The following describes preparation for extending the assignment in a separate project. Use JSX in a separate React Vite project. Record compatible major versions of React and @react-three/fiber, the Three.js version, and the lockfile. This course uses stable WebGL-based APIs and does not mix in alpha WebGPU APIs. Handle frame updates with useFrame and ref.
values.concepts.0.title: Canvas Area
values.concepts.0.explanation: Canvas determines its rendering area from the size of its parent element. Without a parent height, the scene may not be visible.
values.concepts.1.title: Field of View
values.concepts.1.explanation: Camera position and fov determine what fits on screen. Changing object size and camera settings together makes it difficult to identify the cause.
values.outcomes.0: The Canvas area updates when the parent size changes.
values.outcomes.1: Record the screen coverage at two fov values in the same viewport.
values.steps.0: Give the Canvas parent a height of 400px in src/App.jsx.
values.steps.1: Set camera position [0,0,5] and fov 50 to view the cube.
values.steps.2: Change the parent width, and separately record the screen with only fov changed to 75.
values.variables.0.name: fov
values.variables.0.expected: At the same distance, the cube appears smaller on screen.
values.criteria.0: The Canvas area updates when the parent size changes.
values.criteria.1: Record the screen coverage at two fov values in the same viewport.
values.questions.0: How do you distinguish a parent height of 0 from an object behind the camera?
values.questions.1: Do changing fov and changing camera distance always have the same effect?

values.concepts.0.title: Constructor Arguments
values.concepts.0.explanation: args passes arguments to a Three.js constructor. Changing args may recreate the object, so distinguish this from a simple transform.
values.concepts.1.title: Property Updates
values.concepts.1.explanation: position, rotation, and scale are transform properties of an existing object. Recreating geometry dimensions and changing scale have different costs.
values.outcomes.0: Changing only scale does not change the geometry uuid.
values.outcomes.1: Record the uuid before and after changing args.
